To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mononuclear cells from healthy subjects and HIV‐infected individuals produce factors that enhance functional activity of PMN from healthy donors.
MNC supernatants (MNC‐SN) from healthy donors and HIV‐infected individuals (at all stages of infection) enhance functional activity of PMN from healthy donors.

MNC from HIV‐inflicted patients produce factors which augment functional activity of PMN from healthy subjects, and that this effect is most pronounced in patients with early stages of the HIV‐infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of factors which augment functional activity of PMN by MNC from HIV‐inflicted patients.
the presence of a factor(s) in MNCS from healthy donors and HIV‐infected subjects which enhance CL of PMN.
the production of factors which enhance functional PMN activity by MNC from HIV‐inflicted patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MNC from healthy donors and from HIV‐infeceted patients produce factors which stimulate PMN CL.

MNCS from HIV patients contain factors which enhance PMN CL and chemotaxis, which are not connected with the presence of IL‐1β or IL‐8 and which may play an important role in the pathogenesis of the immunodeficiency syndrome.
the observed effects of MNCS on PMN function are probably due to the production of a factor which is not IL‐1β or IL‐8, and which is produced by both healthy donors and HIV‐infected subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MNCS from healthy donors and HIV‐infected individuals have the capacity to enhance functional activity of PMN.
MNC from HIV‐inflicted individuals produce factors that enhance PMN functional activity, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of HIV infection.
MNCS from HIV patients contain a factor(s), which enhances PMN CL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MNC from HIV‐infec‐ted patients produce factors which can enhance functional activity of PMN from healthy subjects.
HIV infection induces a production of a soluble factor by MNC which augments the functional activity of PMN.
MNCS from healthy and HIV‐infected donors contain a factor(s) which enhances PMN functional activity.
